title: To a Statue of a Nude Woman
text:
Naked and vertical, but girded,

the line of the earth to the indolence

        of a flesh that yields, when the perfection

of dream begins its measure.


Matter without love, but kindled

by the faithful number of purity,

        where cold flesh is dressed

without the taste of time and life.


O docile to the eyes and set apart

from the fire of blood, mute glory

        in ecstasy of lifted earth!


Ancient youth, fresh and worn,

that afflicts the passion of its memory

        in this eternity so calm.
editorial_note: The source catalog title differs, but the body is the nude-statue sonnet; the translation preserves its sculptural restraint.

title: How Your Burning Sap Flows
text:
Radiance joins us in this bonfire

that your alabaster makes transparent and gilds,

and in most joyful tongues devours

a vineyard of dead spring.


Stars of swiftest course

slide in your eyes, and all your being

explores me as a tempting ember,

the heart that waits consumed.


Beloved without secret, so near,

I see you intimate and open, in a sunset

that the sun makes within yourself, how


your burning sap flows beneath clean satin;

and I make a vine shoot of my love, which wins

gold for the thirst in which I burn.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the erotic vineyard, alabaster, sap, satin, and burning thirst.

title: Memory
text:
And trembling love slipped

along the mute shores of your absence.

Night became the body of your essence,

and the open field folded, defeated.


A yesterday of your lips in my ear,

a sonorous footprint, a cadence,

made your presence a flower of heartbeats

at the final edge of forgetting.


You came upon an air of poppies.

Like sighs bursting red,

beneath the ardor of the full stars,


the lips advanced like waves.

And submissive in the dream of your eyes,

pain died in the flowering veins.
editorial_note: The translation keeps memory as sound, flower, red sigh, and pain dying in the beloved's gaze.

title: To the Millstone
text:
The straight course of imprisoned water

became circle and song in your ardors,

bread of rock, in your miller's dance,

my murmurs happy with your dawns.


Sun of ears of wheat, your turning lips,

lips of weeping, light heaviness,

silence your bitter spring,

dead moon in the weeping of flowers.


Today I look at you, rest of the road,

coin of abandoned memory

in the quiet nostalgia of the mill.


Sad Cyclops, the eye without a gaze

and the walking form without destiny,

pierced through the axis of the air.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the millstone as circular song, dead moon, abandoned coin, and sad Cyclops.
